# AzureDeck 1.9.12 — Bloxstrap-managed launching

Every game launch/rejoin now starts %LOCALAPPDATA%\Bloxstrap\Bloxstrap.exe directly. Windows resolves LocalAppData for the current user on each device; no username is hard-coded. Install and finish Bloxstrap setup there first. Launch & recovery includes its official download link and an Open launcher folder button. There is no direct-player or stock-installer fallback.

Before requesting an account ticket, AzureDeck runs Bloxstrap's no-launch update check and validates its managed Player bundle. Successful preparation is cached for 60 seconds. It then requests a fresh account-specific ticket and sends one escaped roblox-player URI to Bloxstrap, retaining public/private-server and specific-instance destinations. Cookies are not passed to Bloxstrap.

Bloxstrap is started suspended, assigned to an owned Windows process job, then resumed. AzureDeck follows self-updater/helper handoffs and adopts a unique stable RobloxPlayerBeta child from Bloxstrap's Versions directory, even while the launcher remains open. It then uses the existing account/place-matched log confirmation for up to 90 seconds. A launcher window/process alone never counts as a joined account. Multi-instance checks, queued selection and Discord commands use this same backend.

Cancelled or timed-out launcher jobs remain tracked. Further launches wait until that work finishes; a late player from a cancelled job is closed without touching unrelated clients. Fatal critical/exception/connectivity dialogs are detected and the failed job is closed automatically. Healthy update writes are allowed to finish after timeout/cancellation. Missing setup, denied process access and timeouts produce explicit results.

Automatic recovery now asks Bloxstrap to update, then uses Bloxstrap's forced Player reinstall if the update or its next client launch still fails. Both attempts are bounded and persist across restart. AzureDeck no longer deletes the Roblox/Bloxstrap folders or runs RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe for recovery. Existing native-installer latches migrate to the new backend once; new Bloxstrap failures remain protected. Bloxstrap itself manages its Player files during update/reinstall.

When Bloxstrap updates and closes older clients, AzureDeck suppresses crash-recovery loops during that operation and rebuilds the selected queue. FPS/potato settings remain available; persistent rendering overrides now use Bloxstrap's Modifications/ClientSettings folder so its launcher can apply them to updated clients. For lower launcher overhead, configure Bloxstrap's own activity tracking/integrations in its settings.

The interface was checked against the official [Bloxstrap 2.11.4 launch parser](https://github.com/bloxstraplabs/bloxstrap/blob/v2.11.4/Bloxstrap/LaunchSettings.cs) and [bootstrapper](https://github.com/bloxstraplabs/bloxstrap/blob/v2.11.4/Bloxstrap/Bootstrapper.cs). Native tests use disposable fake launchers/players. Official and installed binary metadata were checked without executing Bloxstrap. Live game joins, private-server access and ten-account native Home login persistence remain unverified; switching launchers cannot guarantee a fix for every Roblox-side error. See VALIDATION.md.
